title: Personal Credit Cards: Purchases, Cash Advances, Balance Transfers and Transaction Fees
content:
Charges on Personal Credit Cards are purchases, cash advances (ATM cash, a cash advance at a bank counter, or a cash-equivalent transaction) and balance transfers from other lenders. This page states when such charges may post and which transaction fees they attract.

## When charges may post

- A purchase, cash advance or balance transfer posts only to a card account whose status is active, as recorded by the bank at the time.
- Authorizing a purchase requires an active account and requires that, once the purchase is added, the balance does not exceed the credit limit enlarged by the tier's tolerance percentage. No over-limit fee is ever charged.
- The cash advances posted in the current statement cycle, taken together by posting date, may not go beyond the tier's cash advance percentage of the credit limit.
- A balance transfer is accepted only on a tier that allows transfers.

## Transaction fees

| Charge | Fee |
|---|---|
| Cash advance | the tier's cash advance percentage applied to the advance and rounded half-up to the cent, or the tier's smallest cash advance fee, whichever is larger |
| Balance transfer | the tier's transfer percentage applied to the amount moved and rounded half-up to the cent, or the tier's smallest transfer fee, whichever is larger |
| Purchase made abroad or in a currency other than US dollars | the tier's foreign transaction percentage of the purchase, rounded half-up to the cent; a tier percentage of 0.00 produces no fee entry |

Each transaction fee is linked to the transaction that caused it and belongs to the same statement cycle as that transaction.

## Rate on a balance transfer

A transfer that posts within the tier's introductory window, counted in calendar days after the account opened, carries the introductory APR until the introductory end date; a transfer posting later carries the purchase APR.

## Rewards

No rewards accrue on cash advances or on balance transfers.

## Rounding illustration (hypothetical percentages)

Suppose a percentage of a cash advance works out to 8.4250 USD: half-up rounding gives 8.43 USD, and that figure is then compared with the tier's smallest fee, the larger of the two being billed. A computation giving 8.4249 USD would round to 8.42 USD instead. The rounding happens on the percentage amount alone, before the comparison with the smallest fee.
